- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–7 days.
- If model shows early downward trend (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling) but sentiment is neutral or positive, model underestimates; add 1–2% upward bias for next 7–14 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and model forecasts are rising, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- Model often underestimates late-period price peaks (last 5–7 days of forecast) — especially if sentiment is positive; add 1–3% upward bias for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.5, 0.0, 0.5), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment peaks 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral or negative, add 0.5–1.5% downward bias for final 10–15 days.
